summary: Friedrich Windischmann (1811–1861) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at LMU Munich and the University of Bonn under Christian Lassen and August Wilhelm Schlegel, later holding posts at LMU Munich and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.

Friedrich Zarncke (1825–1891) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University from circa 1843 to 1847, and later held academic posts at the University of Rostock (around 1848–1850) and Leipzig University (around 1850–1891).

Friedrich von Spiegel (1820–1905) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn under Christian Lassen, and under Hermann Brockhaus and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer. He was a professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1849–1890).

Frits Staal (1930–2012) worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam, Banaras Hindu University, and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. He held posts at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Amsterdam, MIT, and UC Berkeley.
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen (1898–1979) was a philosopher who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1919–1923). He held academic posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1936–1941) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1947–1969).

Fu-shih Lin (1960–2021) worked in history, archaeology, religious studies, and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and served at Academia Sinica's Institute of History and Philology (~1994–2021).

Fujio Taniguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, also studying under several other teachers, and held a post as a lecturer at Chiba College of Health Science.

Fumihiko Sueki (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Fumimaro Watanabe (1934–1990) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, Nagoya University, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Fumimasa Fukui (1934–2017) worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville and Akira Hirakawa. He was a professor at Waseda University (~1978–1989).
Fumio Enomoto (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professor posts at Kyoto University from circa 1983 to 1990 and at Osaka University from circa 1999 to 2002.

Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1949–1957), Shizuoka University (~1957–1968), Taisho University (~1968–1973), and Tsuru University (~1975–1983).

Fumio Matsuda works in religious and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University until 1999 and served as an executive committee chair for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions around 1997.

Fumio Ouchi (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University, earning a doctorate in literature, and held a post there as an assistant professor.

Fumio Shoji (born 1979) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University (~1998–2007) and later served there as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~2012–2017).
Fumio Tamamuro (born 1935) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University from circa 1954 to 1962 and later held a post there from circa 1971 to 2006.
Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College in 1998 and served as a lecturer at Kyushu University.

Futoshi Takehashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Otani University (~1987–1992) and held an assistant post at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute of Teaching from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tsarskoye Selo Lyceum, Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev, and under Georg Bühler, later holding a post at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1941).
